entries.title: Hebrews 9:12
segments: His own blood. The high priest, cleanses symbolically by the blood of animals, entered the Holy of Holies to atone for the people.  Christ by his voluntary sacrifice on the cross entered heaven, having made atonement once for all for sin. See

entries.title: Hebrews 9:14
segments: Dead works. All works done in a slavish spirit, merely to comply with legal requirements, are dead.

entries.title: Hebrews 9:15
segments: Transgressions that were under the first covenant. God was merciful to those who died before Christ came.  The virtue of his reconciling sacrifice extends back to the Old Testament saints who lived in faith, looking forward to a perfect revelation of God's love in Christ.

segments: Testament. A will.

entries.title: Hebrews 9:20
segments: Blood of the covenant. Covenants sealed with blood were common in the early age of the Jewish people.  Often in the Middle Ages of Europe men signed covenants with their blood. This added to the sacredness and surety of the contract.  So God's covenant with his people was sealed with the blood of clean animals, symbolizing the voluntary sacrifice of Christ which sealed his final covenant with man.

entries.title: Hebrews 9:22
segments: Shedding of blood. Blood was the symbol of life, and underneath the whole Jewish ritual was the idea that the life of men was forfeited to God because of sin. Blood, representing life, was therefore offered in sacrifice as an atonement for sins.  See

entries.title: Hebrews 9:23
segments: Heavenly things. The spiritual sanctuary into which Christ has gone, with its heavenly realities corresponding to the symbols of the Levitical sanctuary.

entries.title: Hebrews 9:24
segments: Before the face of God. That is, in the immediate presence of God instead of in the Holy of Holies of an earthly and temporary tabernacle, which was only a symbol of that presence.  Moreover, Christ's mediation for all mankind is continuous, eternal (Heb 7.25); the Levitical high priest appeared in behalf of the Jewish people only once a year.  Humanity, therefore, is ever present in the compassionate mind of the risen Christ, who is in the eternal presence of the father.

entries.title: Hebrews 9:28
segments: So Christ also. Death also ended the earthly part of Christ's mission as the revealer of God to mankind and the Saviour from sin, he awaits the fruits of his work, the people, and so apart from sin he shall come again.
